extra.message: User-controlled query parameter 'name' is interpolated into an f-string 'content' (line 38) and then passed to jinja2.Template(content).render() (line 41). Because the user input becomes part of the template source itself, an attacker can inject Jinja2 template expressions such as {{7*6}} or {{config}} / {{ ''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__() }} to achieve Server-Side Template Injection, leading to information disclosure and remote code execution. The commented-out test in tests/test_main.py ({{7*6}}) confirms this attack surface.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: The user-controlled 'name' query parameter (and the externally fetched 'public_ip') are concatenated directly into an HTML response string without any output encoding/escaping, and the result is returned as an HTMLResponse. An attacker can supply a value such as ?name=<script>alert(1)</script> to inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript into the page, resulting in reflected Cross-Site Scripting.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: A secret token is hardcoded directly in source: SUPER_SECRET_TOKEN = "5u93R53Cr3tT0k3n". Hardcoded credentials/secrets committed to source code can be extracted by anyone with repository access and cannot be rotated without a code change. It should be loaded from an environment variable / secret manager instead.

A value treated as a secret (SUPER_SECRET_NAME = "John Ripper") is hardcoded in source code rather than being loaded from an environment variable as the FIXME comment indicates. Hardcoded secret values in source control are exposed to anyone with repository access.
